senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; preced.) yoke; a pair of working animals tied to the yoke.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 5:1">B. Bath. V, 1</cite> <he>מבר … את הצ׳ הבקר</he> if one sold ‘a yoke’, he has not sold the oxen (but only the yoke); <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 5:1">ib.</cite> <he>אמר מכור לי צִמְדְּךָ וכ׳</he> (Bab. ed. 77ᵇ <cite ref="R00383"><he>צִימְ׳</he></cite>) if he said, sell me thy yoke for two hundred Zuz, it is well known that a yoke is not worth two hundred Zuz (therefore he meant the yoke of oxen); v. <cite ref="R00371"><he>צִימְדָּא</he></cite>; Tosef. ib. IV, 1.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 116a:3">B. Mets. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>צ׳ של פרות</he> a pair of cows with the yoke, Rashi (Tosaf. a yoke for cows, consisting of two pieces).—
<cite ref="Kiddushin 74b">Kidd. 74ᵇ</cite> <he>מצִמְדָּהּ</he> Var. in Ar. s. v. <cite ref="R00078"><he>צד</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="V00072"><he>תַּבְרָא</he></cite>.
